chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durost, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abi al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both)

He said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of God, I have taught my son how to write. In what trade should I place him?' He replied, 'Place him with God, your father, but do not place him in five [trades]: do not place him as a seller of shrouds, nor as a goldsmith, nor as a butcher, nor as a grain merchant, nor as a slave trader.' He said, 'O Messenger of God, and what is the seller of shrouds?' He said, 'He is the one who sells shrouds and wishes for the death of my community, and the newborn from my community is more beloved to me than all that the sun rises upon.' As for the goldsmith, he exploits the deception of my community. As for the butcher, he slaughters until mercy leaves his heart. As for the grain merchant, he hoards food from my community, and it is more beloved to me that God meets the servant as a thief than that He meets him having hoarded food for forty days. As for the slave trader, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me and said, 'O Muhammad, indeed the worst of your community are those who sell people.'

key_terms.سَبَّاء: Seller of shrouds for the dead

ai.seo_question: What are the five undesirable professions in Shia hadith and why are they discouraged?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Khisal, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) identifies five trades as spiritually detrimental due to their impact on the heart and community: selling shrouds (associated with wishing for death), goldsmithing (financial deception), butchery (hardening of the heart), grain trading (hoarding), and slave trading (exploiting humans). This classification reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on how specific professions can erode moral character (akhlaq) and facilitate social injustice, linking occupational ethics to spiritual well-being.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-45 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, on the authority of Durost, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid, on the authority of Abil Hassan Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim (MGB), “A man went to see the Prophet (MGB) andsaid, ‘O Prophet of God! I have taught my son how to write. What should he engage in now?’ The Prophet (MGB) replied, ‘Have him do any job but the following five: selling shrouds for the dead; working as a goldsmith ; slaughtering quadrupeds; selling wheat; and selling slaves. The reason behind this is as follows. One who sells shrouds for the dead would wish the death of his people, while even a baby from my followers is superior to all the people on the Earth in my sight. A goldsmith would plan to have the people lose their money. When a slaughterer of quadrupeds kills the quadrupeds, he will not forgive others wholeheartedly. A wheat-seller would hoard up the wheat and withhold it from my followers. It would be better if one has stolen something when he meets God, than having hoarded up food for forty days (in order to sell it at a higher price). Selling slaves is a bad job since once Gabriel descended to me and said, ‘Those who sell slaves are the worst people amongst your followers.’’”
